articles.title: US stocks: S&P 500, Nasdaq close lower as Nvidia woes and rate-hike bets pressure US market
articles.summary: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended lower on Friday as Nvidia-related concerns weighed on technology stocks, while the latest inflation data did little to change expectations for further Federal Reserve rate hikes.The S&P lost 31.53 points, or 0.42%, to end at 7,560.87 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 230.13 points, or 0.91%, to 25,135.96. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 46.14 points, or 0.09%, to 52,343.23.Nvidia's shares fell and recorded their sixth straight week of declines, their longest streak since October 2012, after CEO Jensen Huang's resignation on Thursday. He stepped down after revelations of extramarital affairs, including a relationship with a businesswoman suspected by the US of spying for China. Nvidia’s board has approached Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor to Huang, the Financial Times reported.The leadership uncertainty has raised questions about the durability of the AI trade because of Nvidia’s central role in the industry’s expansion and its financial ties to several companies in the sector. AI stocks have been a main driver of the equity bull market.Also Read: Fed officials signal further rate hikes as inflation remains elevated“The tech trade, the AI trade, Nvidia is going to go through a period of volatility, and you’re going to see the bulls and bears kind of wrestle on where this narrative goes through the rest of the year ... there’s been a loss of confidence,” said Anthony Saglimbene, chief market strategist at Ameriprise Financial in Troy, Michigan, according to Reuters.“The market and investors are trying to navigate what the AI theme looks like in the absence of Jensen Huang, who was basically the AI champion and willing to use Nvidia’s balance sheet to fund a lot of this AI expansion. That’s gone.”Despite the recent volatility, all three major indexes were on track to post weekly gains. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set to end four-week losing streaks.The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 3.7%, with Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom among the biggest drags.AI cloud companies CoreWeave and Nebius also declined, while data-centre-related stocks IREN and Applied Digital traded lower.The losses came ahead of Anthropic’s highly anticipated initial public offering next week, which could test demand for established AI companies as investors consider shifting money toward the new entrant.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe S&P 500 technology index fell 1.6%, making it the worst-performing of the benchmark’s 11 major sectors. Microsoft edged 0.4% higher as a global outage affecting products including Outlook and Teams began to ease.The Labor Department said US producer prices rose slightly less than expected in October but increased 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest annual gain since November 2022.The data did little to change expectations for a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least 25 basis points in December. Markets were also pricing in a roughly 10% chance of a larger 50-basis-point move, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Comments from several Fed officials this week suggested the central bank could consider a more aggressive path of rate increases as inflation pressures intensify.San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said Friday that her “bias” was that the central bank would need to raise its policy rate. Boston Fed President Susan Collins also said tighter monetary policy was coming because inflation remained high.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. articles.title: Fed officials signal further rate hikes as inflation remains elevated
articles.summary: Federal Reserve policymakers signalled that further interest-rate increases are likely as stubborn inflation and rising business costs threaten to keep price pressures elevated, Reuters reported.San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said her “bias” was that the central bank would need to raise its policy rate, particularly because services inflation was moving in the wrong direction and showing signs of persistence.“We’re going to need to, in all likelihood, raise rates; I will deliberate this with my colleagues in December at our meeting and in all future meetings and make the collective decision that we judge is most appropriate for the economy that is evolving,” Daly said at a University of Nevada, Las Vegas Center for Business and Economic Research forecast event.The core Consumer Price Index, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, has risen about 0.3% month over month in each of the past three months. That is well above the monthly increase of 0.2% or less that would be consistent with the Fed’s 2% annual inflation target.Daly said she was particularly concerned that services inflation excluding housing was “not moving in the correct direction,” as that category tends to be persistent.“That’s a place where you might think a retailer, or a professional business, if they have to buy more expensive IT goods, pay higher energy bills and have other inputs that are rising in price, might pass that along to customers,” she added.The Fed raised its benchmark rate by a quarter percentage point in September before holding it at a range of 3.75% to 4% in October. Markets widely expect quarter-point increases at the Fed’s December 8-9 and January 26-27 meetings, although Governor Christopher Waller has raised the possibility of a half-point move in December.Daly did not comment specifically on the timing of future increases but said markets understood that the Fed adjusts rates in response to changing economic conditions.She is also monitoring consumer spending closely ahead of the December meeting.Collins sees tighter policy aheadBoston Fed President Susan Collins also said further tightening was needed because inflation remained high, suggesting that rates may have to rise more than she previously expected.“I think it’s clear the direction that monetary policy needs to go and I would think that soon some additional firming, tightening of policy is appropriate,” Collins said in an interview with Bloomberg Television.Recent inflation data have been unfavourable and indicate that price pressures are spreading across the economy, Collins said. “I think it may be that a bit of a tighter policy path than I had pencilled in a couple of months ago might be appropriate.”Collins declined to specify how quickly rates should rise or how high they should go.“I don’t want to get ahead in terms of how high we should go or how fast,” Collins said, adding that her “best-case scenario” is for “a careful adjustment of policy.” She acknowledged, however, that “there are scenarios where I might think about that somewhat differently.”Speaking while attending a housing conference hosted by the Boston Fed, Collins said restoring price stability was essential to a healthy housing sector, even if tighter policy caused some near-term pain. She also said financial markets appeared to be functioning well.Logan calls for stronger market-support toolsDallas Fed President Lorie Logan said inflation was too high and monetary policy needed to become more restrictive. Earlier in the week, she argued for at least two additional quarter-point rate increases, potentially in quick succession.Logan also said the US Treasury market was functioning “very well” despite bouts of interest-rate volatility and that banks had improved their access to emergency funding over the past three years.However, she called on the Fed to strengthen its tools for supporting Treasury-market functioning and providing liquidity to banks without working against monetary policy.“Especially in an economic environment where tighter policy appears necessary, I believe it is prudent for the FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) to strengthen its tools for supporting market functioning without providing unnecessary economic stimulus,” Logan said at a Dallas Fed conference on bank funding.Logan, a former head of open-market operations at the New York Fed, said no intervention was currently needed. She warned, however, that intervening during a monetary-policy tightening cycle could complicate the Fed’s communications.“Historically, the Fed’s interventions to support market functioning have come at times when the FOMC also wanted to stimulate economic activity,” she said. “The same asset purchases could serve two purposes: providing monetary policy accommodation and supporting market liquidity.”“If Treasury market dysfunction emerged now, the FOMC would not have the luxury of using the same asset purchases to accomplish two goals,” Logan said.Logan further said that the banks had improved their access to contingent funding, which provides liquidity during periods of market stress, but should continue preparing to use facilities such as the Fed’s discount window.As services such as FedNow and private-sector payment systems expand, banks could face liquidity needs during weekends and holidays. With the Fed planning to extend its Fedwire Funds wholesale payment system to Sundays and weekday holidays, Logan said discount-window operations should also be expanded.“This is not a change any one Reserve Bank can make on its own,” she said. “I look forward to discussions with my colleagues about this possibility.”Logan also urged the Fed to develop the ability to centrally clear its repurchase, or repo, operations. “This would reduce the balance sheet costs of intermediation,” she said. “Funding from the Fed could then flow more efficiently to the broad market.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

Why Indians behave better at sacred sites
articles.summary: The tranquil and indescribably beautiful environs of Kamarpukur and Joyrambati, the birthplaces of Sri Ramkrishna Paramhansa and Maa Sarada Devi in the verdant plains of West Bengal, are truly balms for the soul. Green-gold vistas of ripening rice fields criss-crossed by a myriad of small rivers and dotted with distant sleepy hamlets greeted the eye as a friend and I headed there from Kolkata. And the early morning autumn sun cast a golden, almost divine glow.It was a world away from the pollution-spewing trucks and buses, factories and warehouses that crowd the suburbs of Kolkata beyond the graceful Vidyasagar Setu arching over the Hooghly. Once the cacophony of the Durgapur Expressway was left behind, there was a perceptible change in mood. Anyone who lives in a frenetic big city these days would vouch that stress is endemic and heading out, away from the madding crowds, leads to an instant lowering of tension.Also Read: Indians splurge Rs 72k cr on their favourite obsessionAnd peace is the overwhelming feeling upon entering the impeccably maintained compounds in both villages that contain not only the quaintly thatched huts where the two elevated souls came into this world, but also prayer halls, offices, bhog areas, dispensaries, guesthouses and flower-filled gardens. Given that thousands - exceeding 20,000 on important days - visit Kamarpukur and Joyrambati daily and stay on for bhog prasad, the compounds' serenity is hard to believe.And their cleanliness stuns. Forget jhalmuri packets, tissue papers or plastic water bottles, not even fallen leaves or dust mar the pathways and gardens. It is not as if there are armies of sweepers on hand to pick up detritus either; visitors are simply more mindful while on the premises. How come? After all Indians these days are notorious for being loud, littering gits, on par with British lager louts. It seems that it all depends on whether places inspire respect and restraint.Also Read: India says foreign goods can overstayIn the expansive hallowed campuses of Kamarpukur and Joyrambati, these same people - Indians - did not talk loudly; they did not try to scratch their initials on pillars; they did not drape themselves on walls or amid the flowers to take selfies; they did not throw trash into the ponds; and they did not let their children turn into screeching, high-speed, wrecking balls. Polite attendants firmly told the few infringers to abide by the rules. And they all willingly complied.I have seen a similar all-pervasive calm at the Belur Math of the Ramakrishna Mission near Kolkata, the Aurobindo Ashram in Pondicherry and the Golden Temple in Amritsar, thousands of miles apart. There are more such places around India where desi visitors are anything but the kind of Ugly Indian Tourist that locals complain about from Goa to Gangtok, Kashmir to Kanyakumari. That just begs the question why Indians are so badly behaved in many other places.An overwhelming majority of those who come to Kamarpukur and Joyrambati are devotees. They, therefore, know the sanctity of those places and behave accordingly. The same is true of the sacred precincts at Belur, Pondicherry and Amritsar. But why is the same courtesy not extended to all places they visit? Do only the divine merit courtesy, cleanliness and calm? The public's behaviour at these places show that Indians can be model visitors when we want to be.At Kamarpukur and Joyrambati it is hard to be anything but ideal visitors, though. There's something about the cumulative effect of their soothing tranquillity broken only by birdsong and trees rustling in the autumn breeze, the fresh flowers artfully arranged around the statues of Sri Ramkrishna and Maa Sarada Devi, and the smiling sanyasis telling stories of the divine couple's limitless humanity and humbleness... On the journey back to Kolkata, our hearts were full.

articles.title: Jensen Huang controversy puts Southeast Asia’s AI chip trade under scrutiny
articles.summary: Chip and data-centre operators in Southeast Asia are bracing for tighter scrutiny after reports linking former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to a Chinese businesswoman suspected of spying for Beijing put Singapore and Malaysia in the spotlight, industry executives and analysts told Reuters.The controversy has prompted US lawmakers from both parties to push for stronger restrictions on China’s access to advanced artificial intelligence chips and intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s role in US national security.Washington already restricts exports of Nvidia’s most advanced AI chips to China to protect US leadership in the sector. Lawmakers are now seeking to close a loophole that allows Chinese companies to rent computing power from overseas data centres and remotely access systems equipped with restricted chips.Any tougher regulations could include new export controls and licensing requirements for shipments to Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, the Wall Street Journal reported.Also Read | Anthropic IPO share orders from China are said to be rebuffedAlice Huang, the businesswoman suspected of spying for China, previously worked as an executive at Singapore-based cloud-computing company Megaspeed. The company has subsidiaries in Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Australia and the US.Singapore authorities have been investigating Megaspeed since February last year over possible false declarations related to server purchases and other alleged offences.“After this case, every operator in the chain will be expected to know its end user. Southeast Asian operators will still get Nvidia chips, but proof of where every chip sits and who it serves is now part of the product,” Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based investment research firm Shenton Research, told Reuters.A ‘post-DeepSeek moment’Southeast Asia’s data-centre industry has grown rapidly as global technology companies expand their AI infrastructure.Malaysia has approved 385.7 billion ringgit ($94.67 billion) of data-centre-related investment since 2021, according to the country’s trade ministry. Thailand had 42 data centres representing 3,400 megawatts of IT capacity and about 750 billion baht ($22.58 billion) of investment as of February, while Indonesia’s market was valued at $2.81 billion in 2025.Gary Goh, CEO of Malaysia-based data-centre consultancy Sprint DC, described the prospect of tighter US rules as a “post-DeepSeek moment.”“Once the new rules are out, there will be a lot more restrictions for countries like Malaysia. There could be a short- to medium-term market shock to the Malaysian data centre market,” Goh said.For live updates on US Markets, click hereThe AI boom has supported economic growth across the region. Singapore raised its annual growth forecast in August to between 4.5% and 5.5%, from 2% to 4%, citing the AI cycle. In Malaysia, an increase in data-centre projects helped the construction sector grow 6% in the third quarter of 2026.The trade ministries of Singapore and Malaysia did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Malaysia said Thursday that it was considering legislation that would allow the government to monitor data-centre operations, including the use of high-performance chips. Authorities said they needed to ensure that chips subject to US restrictions were imported for domestic use rather than re-exported.An investor and CEO of an Asian neocloud company, who asked not to be identified, said he spent Friday morning consulting lawyers in the US.“Everyone is still figuring out... Maybe every time you export something, there will be additional process to go through. We are worried about more scrutiny which will make it longer for chips to come through,” the CEO said.Singapore said in February 2025 that entities operating in the country accounted for 22% of Nvidia’s chip sales, although only 1% of the chips physically entered Singapore. Authorities have also charged a fifth person in a case involving alleged AI-server fraud.Region expected to withstand tighter rulesSome analysts said tighter controls were unlikely to derail the data-centre expansion in Singapore and Malaysia.“Singapore itself will be more stringent; I think it’s a natural thing to happen. Singapore will tighten rules, and the US will tighten rules, but I don’t think this will harm Singapore’s and Malaysia’s prospects of buying chips,”  Jarick Seet, head of small- and mid-cap equities at Maybank, told Reuters.A senior executive at a Singapore chipmaker, who declined to be identified, said Huang’s departure could make it more difficult for Chinese companies to obtain US chips while potentially improving availability elsewhere.“With Jensen out, the Chinese will have a harder time getting chips from the US. Maybe it is not a bad thing for the non-US people who will have more access to chips.”The executive said companies could also redirect investment to Southeast Asia if Democratic electoral victories in data-centre-heavy US states such as Texas and Georgia slow the development of new facilities.“Those companies are going to look elsewhere and likely come to countries that can offer them land and deals and power,” the executive said. “Even if we lose a chunk of the China business, I think we will get other companies coming looking for compute.”(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

articles.title: India says foreign goods can overstay
articles.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)  introduced greater flexibility for foreign businesses and organisations on Friday, bringing goods into India temporarily by allowing senior customs officials to extend the existing four-month stay limit under the ATA Carnet system.The move will benefit foreign exhibitors, businesses, media organisations and other international participants who need to bring equipment, commercial samples or professional goods into India for a limited period. Until now, such goods were generally required to be re-exported within four months of their import.Under the revised provision, Principal Chief Commissioners of Customs and Chief Commissioners of Customs can approve an extension beyond the four months if they consider it necessary in the public interest.However, the extended period cannot go beyond the validity of the respective ATA Carnet."Provided also that where the Principal Chief Commissioner of Customs or the Chief Commissioner of Customs, as the case may be, is satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest so to do, may extend the aforesaid period of four months by such further period as it may deem fit, not exceeding the period of validity of the A.T.A. Carnet," said a memo from the Department of Revenue.What changes under the revised ATA Carnet rules?The amendment gives senior customs officials the authority to grant additional time for temporarily imported goods to remain in India.Previously, the four-month limit applied under the relevant customs notification, leaving limited room for businesses and organisations that needed more time before sending their goods back.With the latest change, the Principal Chief Commissioner or Chief Commissioner of Customs can assess individual cases and allow an extension where circumstances justify it.The additional time will depend on the official's assessment, but there is one important restriction: the extension must remain within the validity period of the ATA Carnet. This means the new provision does not allow goods to stay in India indefinitely.The amendment has been made to Notification No. 4/2018-Customs, dated January 18, 2018, by inserting an additional proviso under condition (vi).What is the ATA Carnet system and how does it work?An ATA Carnet is an international customs document that allows goods to enter a country temporarily without the importer having to pay customs duties at the time of import, subject to compliance with the applicable conditions.Often described as a passport for goods, the document simplifies customs procedures for businesses and individuals transporting professional equipment, commercial samples and exhibition materials across international borders.The system is particularly useful for companies participating in overseas trade fairs, exhibitions and business events. It also helps media organisations and professionals who need to carry specialised equipment across countries for temporary assignments.However, the duty-free facility comes with an important condition: the goods must be re-exported within the permitted period.

articles.summary: Microsoft outage today: Outlook users not able to access emails during the Microsoft 365 outage should resist the urge to reset their passwords/ reinstall Office. These fixes may seem worth trying when an inbox suddenly stops working but they won't help as Microsoft's services are down.MQTec Managing Director Moneeb Qureshi has warned users against making unnecessary changes to their Outlook accounts and software while Microsoft works to address the disruption.Microsoft outage began on Thursday affecting "Exchange Online". Outlook users experienced problems accessing their mailboxes through desktop, web and mobile applications, while email delivery was delayed.Outlook Not Working: Experts Say Leave Your Account Settings AloneA sudden Outlook error doesn't mean something is wrong with your password or computer. During a wider Microsoft 365 outage, the problem is beyond a user's control.Qureshi advised against resetting passwords, rebuilding Outlook profiles or changing DNS, proxy and sign-in settings without a specific reason. Unnecessary changes could leave users with additional configuration problems even after Microsoft restores its services.Checking Microsoft's public service status page is a better first step. Administrators can also look at the Service health section of the Microsoft 365 admin centre for updates.135804339Microsoft 365 Problems Extend to Teams and SharePointThe outage has affected more than email. While Teams chats, calls & meetings remained available. But calendar functions, scheduling & invitations faced problems.SharePoint users could still access files, although external file sharing was affected. Copilot, To Do & Planner also experienced unreliable loading. Some Defender and Purview security features operated with limitations.Microsoft's initial investigation found that an unexpectedly large number of servers had become unavailable and increased pressure on the remaining infrastructure. Microsoft said there was no indication of an attack.Are Outlook Emails Being Lost During the Microsoft OutageDelayed emails are not necessarily lost. And email systems generally try to deliver messages again when the receiving server becomes available.As per MQTec, Microsoft extended Exchange Online's normal 24 hour delivery window to 48 hours during the disruption, allowing delayed messages more time to reach recipients.Qureshi advised users not to resend emails. But they should do so only after receiving a non-delivery report confirming that the original message failed.135802371How to Keep Business Communications Running As Microsoft Is DownMQTec recommends that businesses have backup communication arrangements rather than relying entirely on Outlook.Emergency email accounts with another provider can help essential employees stay in touch during an outage. Businesses can also consider email continuity services that retain incoming messages until Microsoft 365 becomes available again.Locally stored data is another option. articles.summary: Fintech major Razorpay Software Ltd has moved a step closer to its stock market debut after receiving approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its initial public offering (IPO), according to an update on the regulator's website.The market regulator issued its final observations on Razorpay's draft offer documents on November 3, clearing the way for the company to proceed with the next stages of its listing process. Renewable energy independent power producer Sembcorp Green Infra also received Sebi's approval, on November 13, the update showed.Razorpay had confidentially filed its draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with Sebi in June. The confidential filing route allows companies to obtain regulatory feedback without immediately making their financial statements and other sensitive business information public.The Bengaluru-based company is working towards a listing in the first quarter of 2027, ET had reported earlier this month. However, the timeline could be pushed back depending on market conditions and investor appetite. The final IPO launch date and pricing will be determined by demand from institutional and retail investors, as well as broader equity market sentiment.ET had reported on April 20 that Razorpay was preparing a confidential IPO filing to raise Rs 5,500-6,500 crore at an expected valuation of around $5 billion, or Rs 49,000-50,000 crore. This would be below the $7.5 billion valuation the company commanded in its last major private funding round in 2021.Subsequently, the fintech has also attracted investor interest at a lower valuation of around $3 billion, or Rs 30,000 crore, reflecting the more cautious approach investors have adopted towards valuations of technology companies ahead of their public listings.Razorpay's shareholders have approved a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 2,700 crore, alongside an offer for sale (OFS) through which existing investors can partially pare their holdings. Axis Capital, JPMorgan, Citi and Kotak Mahindra Capital are advising the company on the proposed IPO.The Sebi approval comes at a time when public market investors are increasingly scrutinising the growth, profitability and valuations of India's new-age technology companies. Walmart-backed payments rival PhonePe had paused its IPO plans earlier this year amid market uncertainty, highlighting the importance of timing for fintech companies looking to tap public markets.ALSO READ: Razorpay gets Sebi nod for Rs 5,000-6,000 crore IPO: sourcesFounded in 2014 by Harshil Mathur and Shashank Kumar, Razorpay provides businesses with online and offline payment acceptance solutions, cross-border payments and a range of financial services. Its investors include Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Tiger Global, Y Combinator and GIC.The company reported a 65% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to Rs 3,783 crore in FY25, compared with Rs 2,296 crore in the previous financial year. However, it posted a consolidated net loss of Rs 1,209 crore, largely due to expenses related to employee stock options, restructuring and tax costs associated with shifting its domicile to India."FY25 was a pivotal year for Razorpay. We delivered top-line growth through strong execution, while simultaneously improving our gross margins," cofounder and chief executive Harshil Mathur had said while announcing the company's financial results.Ahead of its proposed listing, Razorpay has also recalibrated its offline payments business, shifting its focus towards merchants that require an integrated online and offline payments offering. articles.summary:
Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran on Friday said monetary policy tools such as interest rate adjustments may become less effective in tackling inflation in a world increasingly vulnerable to supply-side disruptions.
"Fiscal and other public policy measures will be more important because raising interest rates will not solve the supply-induced problems. If anything, it may even be counter-productive," he said at the 9th Annual Food Systems Dialogue here.

articles.title: Sensex, Nifty's explosive rally pushes market to pre-Middle East war levels. How long will they take to scale fresh peaks?
articles.summary: The return of FIIs and easing oil prices sparked a skyrocketing rally in the Indian stock market this month, pushing the benchmark indices to levels not seen since the Middle East war ensued earlier this year, but analysts say it may take a few more months for them to hit fresh lifetime highs.Sensex this week touched 82,000, marking the first time since last February before US-Israel’s joint air strikes killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, beginning a conflict that sparked a sharp surge in oil prices and spooked investors, continuing till date. Nifty traded above 25,350 before the infamous March selloff began. The index has now traced its way back above the level.Also read |Sensex erases all Middle East war losses but is it too soon to forget the Hormuz factor?How far are Sensex, Nifty from their lifetime highs?Despite the recent gains, the benchmark indices are sharply down from their respective lifetime lows. Sensex had hit a lifetime high of 86,159 on December 1 last year, and Nifty had hit an all-time high of 26,373 early in January this year. The benchmark indices are around 5% away from their respective record peaks despite the recent rally.Sensex has recovered over 11,000 from its recent low to hover near 81,900, which leaves 86,000 about 5% away. Vaqarjaved Khan, Senior Fundamental analyst at Angel One, feels that this rally has fundamental support. Earnings visibility is improving, banking, autos and consumption are showing healthier demand, and softer input costs are helping margins, he said, adding that steady SIP flows from domestic investors also give the market a cushion even when foreign money turns cautious. Sensex’s recovery of over 11,000 points from its October low reflects a sharp improvement in market sentiment, supported by renewed foreign institutional inflows, easing crude oil prices and encouraging corporate earnings, said Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura. Why caution is warranted after such sharp spikeHowever, after such a steep rally, some consolidation and profit booking cannot be ruled out, the analyst said. While the broader market outlook remains positive, geopolitical uncertainties, inflationary pressures and fluctuations in foreign capital flows could create intermittent volatility, according to Bolinjkar. “We expect the next leg of the rally to be increasingly driven by earnings growth rather than liquidity alone.”“I would not call valuations comfortable after such a sharp run. Earnings need to catch up with prices, and that is what I will be watching in the coming quarters. Crude oil, global cues and foreign inflows will decide how quickly we move,” Khan from Angel One said.The current rally has been driven by falling crude levels, the return of foreign money and better-than-expected earnings. All three need to hold, and none of them is guaranteed while the US-Iran situation remains unresolved and the Fed stays hawkish, said Tanvi Kanchan, Associate Director at Anand Rathi Shares & Stock Brokers. She noted that the market is already showing signs of fatigue near these levels as the Sensex has slipped back from its November 11 high and has been trading in a narrow range on Thursday.Also read | Rs 80,000 crore FII buying sparks explosive rally on Dalal Street. Will RBI rate hike worries kill the party?When could Sensex, Nifty soar back to lifetime highs?A fresh lifetime high, which is sustainable, is a realistic possibility over the next few months rather than the next few sessions, provided crude stays contained and foreign flows remain positive, one can expect short term consolidation before the breakout, according to Kanchan from Anand Rathi.Khan from Angel One has a base case that the Sensex can cross 86,000 and set a fresh lifetime high in roughly three to six months, provided Q3 FY27 earnings hold up and there is no external shock. “I would advise investors not to chase the rally and to accumulate quality large caps on dips.”Ventura analyst Vinit Bolinjkar believes that Sensex could test the 86,000–86,200 zone over the next two to three months, provided foreign inflows remain strong, crude prices stay contained and corporate earnings sustain their momentum. “A decisive breakout above the immediate resistance of 82,500 could pave the way towards 84,000 and eventually 86,000,” he said.Sudeep Shah, Head of Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said if the market succeeds in holding on to its bullish momentum, Sensex could potentially revisit its lifetime highs over the next 3-6 weeks. “However, investors should not expect the rally to be linear. After such a sharp recovery, intermittent profit-booking and consolidation would be healthy and could provide a stronger base for the next leg of the uptrend,” according to Shah.Ajit Mishra, SVP of Research at Religare Broking, meanwhile believe Sensex is well positioned to reclaim the 86,000 mark and potentially surpass its previous lifetime high over the next 3-6 months. However, the next leg of the rally will need earnings delivery rather than just valuation re-rating, he said, adding that investors should use intermittent corrections to accumulate fundamentally strong businesses with sustainable growth prospects.Also read |MSCI rejig: LIC, Meesho, Coforge set to gain from index inclusion. It sold around 400,000 tonnes of chrome valued at about Rs 718 crore and 1.54 million tonnes of coal valued at Rs 175 crore.The company’s e-commerce vertical remains its core growth driver. "This may be the reason for this accident, as the brakes may not have been applied when the FP/BP angle cock of the loco was in an isolated condition," a joint note prepared by the probe team on the day of the accident said.
It further stated that the train crew applied the brakes, "but the brakes may not have been applied as the angle cock was previously in the closed position".

articles.title: Jensen Huang’s Nvidia exit raises fears over the future of AI financing
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s departure on Thursday raised concerns not only about the future of the multitrillion-dollar chipmaker but also about its willingness and ability to continue financing the artificial intelligence boom, Reuters reported.Huang’s exit added another pressure point to one of the global market’s most crowded trades. It came after Nvidia’s board met late Wednesday to consider the longtime CEO’s future following reports of two extramarital affairs.Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent successor, the company said in a statement.Investors initially sold Nvidia shares and stocks linked to the company, including data-centre operator CoreWeave and South Korea’s Naver. Shares of chipmaking rivals Broadcom and Advanced Micro Devices advanced.Chinese graphics-processing-unit makers also rallied on expectations that Nvidia’s leadership upheaval could help local suppliers gain market share. Moore Threads, MetaX and Cambricon each surged nearly 10%.Nvidia shares fell 13%, while Nasdaq 100 futures declined 0.6%.The broader concern is that Nvidia could scale back its strategy of financing data centres under new leadership, potentially slowing investment across the AI industry.Also Read | Anthropic IPO: Can Indian investors apply for Claude maker's $64 billion share sale? Check rules“Nvidia has been called the ‘Bank of AI’. They’ll sell you the chips and loan you the money. If they have to take a step back because of what’s going on, will that cut off funding to smaller companies that need it? That’s an open question,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey, according to Reuters.Nvidia has been the flagship stock of the AI revolution. Its technological lead and surging sales have driven its share price up about 900% in the four years since the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT helped usher in the generative-AI era.The company has also emerged as a major financier of the industry, investing billions of dollars in customers through equity stakes and other financial commitments as it anticipates growing demand for increasingly powerful chips.“Nvidia’s credit support is what makes much of this debt finance-able across the AI hyperscaler deal front,” said Christopher Brown, senior vice president, investments, at Synovus Securities. “Lenders will ask what happens to that support if Nvidia’s leadership or regulatory standing is impaired, and Nvidia’s own willingness to extend more guarantees may be constrained.”Nvidia’s board launched an investigation into Huang after reports that he had an affair with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy. A separate report involving another alleged affair emerged before Wednesday’s board meeting.Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters that Nvidia’s revenue was unlikely to fall suddenly following Huang’s departure. The greater concern, he said, was the company’s long-term direction because of Huang’s central role in shaping its computing strategy.“Replacing that strategic vision ... is an enormous challenge,” Boloor said.Nvidia’s departure reverberates across AI stocksHuang’s exit creates a leadership vacuum at the roughly $4 trillion company he co-founded and built over more than three decades. Nvidia has become the leading supplier of AI chips and a focal point of the technology rivalry between the United States and China.Asian chip stocks, which had rallied alongside Nvidia during the AI spending boom but recently came under pressure from concerns about financing costs and demand, also declined.Nvidia disclosed $164.5 billion in financial commitments in its latest earnings report. These included an obligation of up to $105 billion tied to an OpenAI data centre in Ohio and more than $50 billion in lease and capacity guarantees.In August, Nvidia said it had partnered with six major financial institutions, including Apollo, BlackRock and Blackstone, to establish computing-finance platforms seeking more than $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. Huang said the company could backstop as much as $125 billion, or 25% of the potential deals.“The interlocking deals that Nvidia has with so much of the industry raise the question of whether that created more stability or more fragility,” Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers, told Reuters.Nvidia is also an investor in Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot. Anthropic’s initial public offering this month is expected to test investor demand for AI-related assets.CoreWeave shares fell more than 7.5% in premarket trading after surging Wednesday on upbeat earnings. Naver, in which Nvidia invested $1 billion by financing a data-centre expansion, dropped 6%.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)
